restamp: Iteration 6 is a re-stamp, not a new change. No file under ui/ was edited between iteration 5 and this: the source hash moved because ui/approvals.js was committed on the branch by another hand (the APPROVALS block now renders a compact policy diff instead of printing the allowlist twice), and the gate hashes the whole --src ui tree. Re-rendered and re-read at 1440, 768 and 390: APPROVALS reads as one line, no wall of addresses, and the panel geometry underneath it is unchanged.

firstFive.what: A terminal trading screen for one Hyperliquid perpetuals account: a live candle chart with the position drawn on it, the book under it, and on the right one risk panel carrying both prices that can end the position, the approvals block, and one time-ordered tape of everything this account has done.
firstFive.who: Someone trading this account with borrowed money, watching a program they armed, who has to decide on the agent's proposals without leaving the price.
firstFive.action: Read the LIQ line, then the tape, then decide the pending proposal or press one of the controls that stops something.

changed_this_iteration.why: Karim, on iteration 4: 'The logs look squished, and I don't like the logs and mandate sections. I want them to be sort of in one, meaning a transaction history and fills as well.' / 'the book of our actual positions and everything is too squished. You can't clearly tell what numbers report what metrics.' / 'a lot of colliding, a lot of conflicting components, and it looks noisy. I don't see truly useful information that I need.'
changed_this_iteration.panels: Eight became five. FILLS, MANDATE and LOG merged into one HISTORY tape. MARKET stopped being a panel and became four ruled lines inside RISK. The armed mandate's live state became a ruled block inside RISK, beneath the liquidation distance it is about.
changed_this_iteration.cut: Open interest and 24h volume (they describe the market's health, never this position's). The per-fill FEE column on the tape. The mandate's stop-out price and last-rule line from the mandate head, both of which moved somewhere they read better: the price up beside the venue's wall, the rule down into the tape.
changed_this_iteration.root_cause: The noise was structural, not painted. Five variable-height panels shared a non-scrolling column whose declared caps summed to 152vh, and `.panel.grow` means `flex-basis: 0`, so the growing panel paid the whole overrun and the log rendered as a frame line with nothing under it. Merging three panels into one removed the competition; capping `.panel-tgate` (style.css only ever capped the pro page's `.panel-gate`) plugged the uncapped one; and a `min-height` floor on the growing panel means it can no longer be shrunk to nothing.

asked.requirement: Components must not collide or conflict, at any width
asked.note: Measured in the browser at 1440, 768 and 390. Page-level sideways scroll is 0 at all three. BOOK and HISTORY both have scrollWidth === clientWidth at 1440 (702/702 and 661/661) and at 768 (728/728), so nothing is off-screen. At 390 both scroll inside their own box (698 in 350, 603 in 350) and the page still does not. This is the requirement that failed at iteration 4: CLOSE POSITION and CANCEL ALL were off the right edge of BOOK whenever a position existed, and the LOG panel rendered as a frame line with zero content whenever a proposal was pending.

asked.requirement: Liquidation distance shown in ATR multiples as well as percent and dollars
asked.note: shot-1440.png: 'LIQ at $713.42, 837.59% away, $841.28, 1607.1 ATR'. The bar under it was WRONG at iteration 4 and is fixed here: liqFill returned `1 - distance/scale`, which clamps to zero for anything far from the wall, so a position 1,607 ATR clear drew a full-red bar meaning 'at your liquidation'. It now returns the distance itself and reads 100% green at that distance, which is what the reverse-meter comment in trade.css always said it should do.

goal.outcome: The three questions the brief names are answered without arithmetic and without looking in more than one place: how far from liquidation, how much of what I approved has been spent, is this screen still telling the truth.
goal.path: RISK is read top to bottom. Collateral, health, then the LIQ line at 16px with the reverse meter under it, then the mandate stop-out on the same scale directly beneath it, then exposure and the 5% sentence, then the instrument, then what is armed and how much of its envelope is gone. Feed health is in the statusbar beside the price. What has already happened is one tape on the right, newest first.
goal.why: shot-1440.png. Distance: 'LIQ at $713.42, 837.59% away, $841.28, 1607.1 ATR' with a full green bar, which now agrees with the sentence above it instead of contradicting it. Envelope: nothing is armed, and the MANDATE block says so in a sentence with a next action. Truth: 'feed LIVE ws 0s' and no banner. The second wall's line renders only when a mandate holds one, so nothing armed leaves no empty row of ground held open for it.

The layout fix for the pending-approval case is verified structurally (a declared cap on APPROVALS and a declared floor on HISTORY) rather than photographically, and the mandate row is unchanged in shape. caveats.what: An opening fill with a venue-reported closedPnl of exactly 0 prints $0.00 on the tape rather than a dash.
caveats.why: Pre-existing and not introduced here: the venue reports the zero, so this is the app repeating what it was told rather than inventing a number for a null. Changing it means changing what src/trade/state.ts treats as unknown, which is outside this change and would move behaviour the trade-state tests assert. Also recorded against requirement 14.
